name: Screensdesign
tagline: A searchable library of real iOS app screens, onboarding flows and paywalls, recorded and broken down screen by screen.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software here is the boring part: a video player, a screen grid, tags, and search. The product is thousands of hours of someone installing apps, recording every flow, cutting them into screens, and labeling what each one is doing. An agent can build you a personal UI reference library in an afternoon, but it cannot go capture 1500 competitor onboarding funnels for you, and your own screenshots folder is not a market survey. If what you want is to see how twelve fitness apps handle their trial paywall, you are paying for the capture labor, not the CRUD. Build the shelf if you like, just know you also have to fill it.
coreLoopDIY: A local library where you drop screen recordings, auto-split them into frames, tag screens by app and pattern, and search or compare them side by side.
requirements: your own screen recordings of apps you actually install
disk space, video is not small
patience for manual tagging, or an image model API key if you want auto-labels
whatYouLose: The corpus: thousands of flows from apps you will never install
Ongoing capture, so you see how a paywall changed over six months
Consistent pattern taxonomy that makes cross-app comparison useful
Curation and editorial picks, the thing that saves you from scrolling forever
Any sense of what the rest of the market is doing, which was the whole point
moatNotes: Capture is manual, repetitive and continuous, which is exactly the kind of moat code does not dissolve. Also worth noting the whole category sits on a soft legal floor: recording other people's paid apps and reselling access to the footage.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because designers are not paying for a video grid, they are paying to skip a week of installing apps, signing up with burner emails, hitting paywalls, and recording it all on a spare phone. The subscription is outsourced labor with a search box on top. It also keeps working when you switch projects: the library already covers the vertical you just moved into, which your personal folder of screenshots does not.
notes: The viewer is a weekend; the footage is not. The moat is the accumulated capture labor plus a pattern taxonomy applied consistently across thousands of flows.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user UI reference library called "shelf" for studying mobile app flows I record myself.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, better-sqlite3, everything on localhost. No auth, no accounts, no cloud storage, no telemetry, no analytics.

Storage layout:
- ./media/recordings for source .mp4 / .mov files I drop in
- ./media/frames for extracted stills
- ./shelf.db for SQLite

Ingest:
- A CLI script `npm run ingest` that scans ./media/recordings for new files, and for each one shells out to ffmpeg to extract frames on scene change (use the scene detection filter, fallback to one frame every 1.5s), writing JPEGs into ./media/frames/{recordingId}/.
- Insert rows: recordings (id, filename, app_name, platform, captured_on, notes), frames (id, recording_id, ts_seconds, path, label, pattern_tags).
- app_name defaults to the filename stem so I can fix it later.

UI:
- / : grid of recordings with a poster frame, app name, frame count.
- /r/[id] : the flow view. Frames in timestamp order as a horizontal filmstrip, click a frame for a large view with the source video seeked to that timestamp, and an inline editor for label and comma separated pattern tags.
- /browse : all frames across all recordings, filterable by app_name and pattern tag, with a "compare" mode that pins up to 6 selected frames side by side on one screen.
- Full text search over app_name, label and tags using SQLite FTS5.
- Keyboard: arrow keys move between frames, `t` focuses the tag input.

Optional and off by default: if OPENAI_API_KEY exists in .env, add a `npm run autolabel` script that sends unlabeled frames to a vision model and fills label plus suggested pattern tags from a fixed vocabulary (onboarding, paywall, signup, empty-state, settings, permission-prompt, upsell, home, detail). Never call it during page renders.

Out of scope, do not build: scraping app stores, downloading anyone else's screenshots, multi-user support, deployment config, mobile app.

Include a README that states plainly that this ships empty and is only as good as the recordings I feed it, plus the exact ffmpeg version assumptions.
